digest.headline: BBC and Channel 4 in talks over potential commercial tie-up
digest.lead: The BBC and Channel 4 have entered preliminary discussions with the UK government regarding a potential merger of their commercial operations. This move aims to combine advertising, streaming services, and specific channels to address broader cost-cutting requirements.

paragraphs: The BBC and Channel 4 are exploring a joint venture that could consolidate their commercial assets. Discussions with the government reportedly include merging Channel 4's advertising business, streaming services, and channels like E4 and Film4 with the BBC's UKTV.
This strategy is part of a wider effort to reduce costs across public service broadcasting. The move follows ongoing financial pressures facing both organisations.

BBC Radio 4 is implementing significant budget reductions, resulting in the cancellation of several long-running programmes. The corporation is cutting its speech audio budget by 10 per cent, leading to the axing of shows including You and Yours.
These changes reflect a broader shift towards podcasting and digital-first content. The cuts are part of a wider 500 million pound savings plan.

Amazon's Prime Video has become the first major streamer to integrate with Barb's CFlight measurement service. This inclusion allows streaming advertising campaigns to be evaluated within the same framework as linear television.

Meanwhile, the BBC is testing an AI-powered redesign for iPlayer to improve personalisation and content discovery. Sky Sports has also launched new accessibility features, including live descriptive audio and subtitles, for its Premier League coverage.

Skydance officially closed its 110 billion dollar acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery on Tuesday. The merger combines major properties from Paramount and Warner Bros into a single entity. David Zaslav received a 606 million dollar payout as he departed the company he led for four years.

The new Skydance structure places DC Comics within a Products and Publishing division. This group also manages consumer products for both Paramount and Warner Bros. Analysts expect Skydance to become a net seller of local CBS stations to manage debt levels.

Amazon has retired the Fire branding for its tablets in favour of the Alexa Tablet name. These new devices include a 12 Pro model designed to compete with the iPad Pro at a lower price point. Crucially, the tablets now support the Google Play store after Amazon killed its own app store.

OpenAI and Meta are competing directly with new AI agents named Dot and Muse. Meanwhile, Amazon announced it will stop using non-disclosure agreements when negotiating data centre deals with local governments. This move follows similar transparency efforts by Microsoft to build community trust.

Ten cable organisations have announced plans to sue the FCC to block the repeal of the broadcast TV ownership cap. The groups want to pause the order which removes the 39 percent national limit. The FCC chair also declined to take a position on the broadcasting of live executions.

In Canada, the CRTC has finalised new Rogers internet speeds for competitors. This follows the completion of the Corus Entertainment recapitalisation which saw the company become a subsidiary of Corus Entertainment Holdings.
